source: Low: FHWA CMF Clearinghouse CMF ID 1966 from Villwock et al. 2009 'Safety Impact of Cable Barriers on Rural Interstates' (head-on/cross-median/opposing sideswipe; all severities). Central: CMF ID 6132 (cross-median; K+A+B+C; original study not captured). High: CMF ID 9846 (cross-median; fatal; Iowa 2007-2015). Locator is the Clearinghouse record; no page or table number.
source_context: USA (Indiana; Iowa; state of 6132 not captured). Rural interstates with wide depressed medians. NOT matched to Indian highways (different median types, vehicle mix and barrier upkeep).
confidence: Low - US interstate cross-median crashes only; studies differ widely (0.09 to 0.38); no Indian evidence.
notes_and_limits: Applies only to cross-median head-on crashes on divided sections with an open median. Does NOT apply to undivided sections, wrong-way entry or head-on at median openings. Barrier strikes can raise other median crashes: Clearinghouse CMF 1.55 for property-damage-only (ID 6133); Russo et al. 2016 report 2.63 for C/O-severity median crashes and 0.76 for K+A median crashes.

intervention: Continuous highway lighting on unlit sections
source: Low: CMF ID 2870 Wanvik 2009 'Effects of road lighting: An analysis based on Dutch accident statistics 1987-2006' (night; A+B+C; rural). Central: CMF ID 192 Elvik & Vaa 2004 'The Handbook of Road Safety Measures' Elsevier (night; A+B+C; meta-analysis). High: CMF ID 193 same handbook (night; property-damage-only). Locator is the Clearinghouse record; handbook page not captured.
source_context: Netherlands (Wanvik) and mainly European meta-analysis (Elvik & Vaa); all road types. NOT Indian-specific.
confidence: Medium - large datasets and a meta-analysis, but European and for unlit-to-lit change only.
notes_and_limits: Night crashes on currently unlit sections only. Does NOT apply to crashes already under street lights (factor 'light_darkness with street lights on' is excluded) and is not shown for twilight or dawn. Range mixes injury (0.46, 0.72) and property-damage-only (0.83) outcomes. CMF 2870 is a 2-star record.

source: CMF ID 433 Elvik & Vaa 2004 'The Handbook of Road Safety Measures' Elsevier (night; A+B+C); Clearinghouse says it is listed in AASHTO Highway Safety Manual 2010 (chapter/table not captured). Low and high = central +/- 1 adjusted standard error (0.13) of the same record: computed from the published SE, not a published low/high.
source_context: International meta-analysis, roadway type not specified (mainly Europe/N. America). NOT Indian-specific.
confidence: Medium - Clearinghouse lists it as a highest-reliability HSM value, but it covers night injury crashes only and is European.
notes_and_limits: Night injury crashes at junctions only; daytime side-impact crashes are not reduced. Needs a junction that is currently unlit. Low/high come from one study's SE, not independent studies: widen if a more cautious range is wanted.

source: Wilson C, Willis C, Hendrikz JK, Le Brocque R, Bellamy N. Speed cameras for the prevention of road traffic injuries and deaths. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews 2010, CD004607 (main results: all crashes near camera sites reduced 8% to 49%, most studies 14% to 25%). Low = 49% reduction; high = 8% reduction; central = midpoint (19.5%) of the 'most studies' range: derived, not a published point estimate.
source_context: Systematic review of 28 crash studies, mainly high-income countries; the review states none were in low-income countries. NOT Indian.
confidence: Low - studies of moderate quality at best, no low/middle-income evidence, central value derived.
notes_and_limits: Effect is measured near camera sites; the review reports smaller effects over wider areas (9% to 35% all crashes). Needs working detection plus penalty follow-up. A Delhi figure (19% fewer fatal accidents, OSVD cameras) appears only in a 2025 NHAI conference slide, not peer reviewed, and is NOT used for the CMF.

source: Low: Shults RA et al. 2001 'Reviews of evidence regarding interventions to reduce alcohol-impaired driving' Am J Prev Med 21(4S):66-88 (median 20% fewer alcohol-related crashes, selective breath testing). Central: a meta-analysis reporting 17% fewer alcohol-involved crashes, as cited in Bergen et al. 2014 (original paper not identified). High: Bergen G et al. 2014 'Publicized sobriety checkpoint programs: A Community Guide systematic review' Am J Prev Med 46(5):529-539 (median 8.9% fewer alcohol-involved fatal crashes).
source_context: USA, Europe, Australia programmes with publicity. NOT matched to Indian enforcement capacity.
confidence: Low - non-Indian, depends on sustained enforcement, outcome definitions differ between the three values.
notes_and_limits: Applies only to alcohol-involved crashes (tv_drunk_driving), not to all crashes. Needs frequent, publicized checkpoints; no effect if not enforced. High value is for fatal alcohol-involved crashes only.

source: Low and central: Merritt D, Lyon C, Persaud B, Torres H. Developing Crash-Modification Factors for High-Friction Surface Treatments. FHWA-HRT-20-061, 2020 (Clearinghouse study ID 599; all-crash CMFs 0.27 and 0.48; which site type each belongs to must be checked). High: CMF ID 7900 Merritt et al. 2015 'Evaluation of Pavement Safety Performance' (individual curve with friction-related crash problem; crash type not confirmed).
source_context: USA (Arkansas, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Pennsylvania, West Virginia and others); curves and ramps; calcined-bauxite surfacing. NOT matched to Indian pavements.
confidence: Low - US curves/ramps only; site type behind each value not confirmed; may not transfer to straight NH sections.
notes_and_limits: Applies only to sites with a friction-related crash problem (curves, ramps, junction approaches). Does NOT cover potholes, drainage or structural failure. 'io_road_condition' is assumed to mean pavement surface condition: confirm with the data team. Wet-road CMFs in the same study are lower (about 0.20 to 0.29) but are not used.

source: Lyon C, Persaud B, Eccles K. Safety Evaluation of Profiled Thermoplastic Pavement Markings. FHWA-HRT-17-075, March 2018 (nighttime wet-road crashes; central = CMF ID 9803; low and high are other nighttime wet-road CMFs listed for the same study, table not captured).
source_context: USA (Florida, South Carolina); rural, mostly two-lane undivided roads. NOT matched to Indian highways.
confidence: Low - small effect, not statistically significant at 95%, based on few crashes.
notes_and_limits: Nighttime wet-road crashes only. The study found no material change in total, fatal+injury or run-off-road crashes, and head-on crashes rose (CMF 1.229, not significant). Does not address fog, dry-night visibility or daytime crashes.

intervention: Fog visibility countermeasures (fog warning or enhanced delineation)
notes_and_limits: No fog-specific CMF was found in the FHWA CMF Clearinghouse or general searches. wx_mist_fog has high lift on several top segments (S043, S046, S049, S053, S067), so show this as an evidence gap, not as zero effect. Do not borrow the wet-night marking CMF (I07) for fog.
